newsitem.title: DENMARK: TELE DANMARK SAYS BELGACOM CHARGE TO CUT H1 RESULT.
newsitem.headline: TELE DANMARK SAYS BELGACOM CHARGE TO CUT H1 RESULT.

text.p: Danish telecoms group Tele Danmark said on Tuesday first half results due on August 29 would show a significant one-off charge related to redundancies in Belgium's Belgacom, in which it has a stake of about 16 percent.

Tele Danmark investor relations chief Henning Rostung declined to say by how much the effect on the results would be, but said his firm had similar accounting practices to U.S. partner Ameritech, which last month announced a charge of $87 million for the Belgacom layoffs.
"Our accounting principles resemble the American practice and our accounts for the first half-year will therefore be significantly affected by the changes in Belgacom," Rostung said.
Ameritech has around a 17 percent holding in the Belgian firm.
Belgacom is to lay off 6,000 workers over 18 months, incurring large redundancy costs.
The Belgian telecoms company is half-owned by a consortium of Tele Danmark, Ameritech, Singapore Telecom and private investors with the Belgian state owning the remaining 50 percent.
Tele Danmark shares closed on the Copenhagen exchange, before Rostung's comments to Reuters, up 1.5 crowns at 390.00.
In New York, they traded at the equivalent of 392.35 crowns per share at 1615 GMT.
